subject: MediStat inference hosting: clarifying compliance constraints & required evidence
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medistat.io>
Cc: Helen Cho <helen@medistat.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & clarifying hosting questions (PHI / BAA / SOC2)

Hi Daniel / Helen —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few items we need to qualify so we can recommend the right hosting route (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

- Use case: inference calls from your EHR connector will include PHI (patient names, DOBs, limited notes). You confirmed this on the call.
- Primary constraint: MediStat requires a signed BAA for any PHI processing and prefers network isolation due to downstream integrations.
- Questions for you (please confirm):
  1) Will you require outbound egress controls (no model telemetry allowed off your VPC)?
  2) Expected token volume and concurrency (ballpark for sizing Dedicated capacity) — daily requests / peak rps.
  3) Required log retention window for audit (audit team expects retention timeframe in days).

Attached: redwood_soc2_onepager.pdf (SOC 2 summary), BAA-draft-20280320.docx (initial BAA we can iterate on), and a hosting_evidence_checklist.xlsx that lists typical artifacts customers request.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- If you need a BAA + Private VPC, we should schedule a 60-min Security & Infra deep-dive (engineers + security) to validate network diagrams and demonstrate encryption controls.
- If you prefer Dedicated capacity (hosted by us with dedicated GPUs and an SLA), we'll need concurrency estimates to size capacity and discuss optional private peering.

Can you confirm the three items above and share a network diagram (or tell us who on your infra team we should loop in)? If convenient, suggest 2x 60-min windows next week and I’ll send an invite.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0163

Attachments (3): redwood_soc2_onepager.pdf (PDF, 120KB); BAA-draft-20280320.docx (DOCX, 45KB); hosting_evidence_checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medistat.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediStat Security <security@medistat.io>, Helen Cho <helen@medistat.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & clarifying hosting questions (PHI / BAA / SOC2)

Aisha —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the quick answers below so you can scope:

1) PHI: yes, the payloads will contain PHI. We cannot tolerate non-consented egress of PHI or patient identifiers.
2) Egress: we require strict egress controls — no telemetry or raw payloads leaving our VPC unless explicitly authorized in writing.
3) Volume: current pilot is ~12k inference calls/day, peak ~5 rps. Production target in 6–9 months is ~120k/day with peaks ~60 rps.
4) Retention: Security requires audit logs for 365 days; application logs can be shorter but audit trail must be preserved.

Preference: given downstream EHR integration and our compliance posture, we are leaning to Private VPC deployment or an on-prem piece. Dedicated (hosted) could be acceptable only if we get private peering, per-tenant encryption keys, and a signed BAA with explicit egress assurances.

Attached: medistat_network_diagram.png (simple sketch of where Redwood would sit relative to our EHR connectors).

Available for the security deep-dive next Tue 2028-03-27 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 2028-03-28 14:00–15:00 PT. Please book the slot that works for your security + infra folks.

On the BAA: please have your legal/security review the draft and we’ll circle back with comments.

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering | MediStat
daniel.park@medistat.io | +1 617-555-2022

Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MediStat hosting questions — quick security assessment

Team — forwarding Daniel's reply and the network sketch. High-level notes from security review:

- Because PHI is in-scope and they insist on no egress, Private VPC (customer-managed network) or an on-prem appliance is the most straightforward path to meet their constraints.
- If we pursue Dedicated with private peering, we must ensure: per-tenant KMS (customer-managed keys), explicit egress controls in the datapath (no telemetry), and verified infrastructure separation (SLA + contract language).
- Audit logs: they request 365-day retention for audit logs. Our hosted plans currently retain detailed audit logs for 90 days by default; we would need to propose an extended retention add-on (cost + storage plan) or show how logs can be exported to their SIEM.
- Action items for Legal (Marcus): review BAA-draft-20280320.docx and propose redlines specific to egress and KMS clauses.
- Action items for SRE/Infra (Sergio): review network diagram and list the changes needed to support Private VPC or to enable Dedicated with private peering. Include network ACLs, encryption-at-rest details, and any additional certs we would need for our endpoints.

Please respond with estimated timelines for your items. I put Aisha on thread so she can coordinate calendar invites.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel / Helen —

Thanks for the confirmation and the diagram — that helps a lot. Based on Daniel's answers and Laura's notes, here's a recommended action plan so we can get a firm recommendation and a preliminary sizing/quote out to you: 

1) Security & Infra deep-dive (60 min) — agenda:
   - Walk the network diagram (15m)
   - Explain our Private VPC and Dedicated with private peering options (15m)
   - Discuss KMS options (customer-managed keys) and egress controls (15m)
   - Confirm audit log retention mechanisms and export pathways (15m)

2) Deliverables from Redwood within 5 business days after the deep-dive:
   - Technical checklist mapping how each option meets their egress + PHI constraints (hosting_evidence_checklist.xlsx)
   - SOC 2 artifacts summary and list of evidence we can provide for audits (redwood_soc2_onepager.pdf)
   - Revised BAA with proposed egress and KMS language (Marcus to provide)
   - Preliminary sizing and cost estimate for Dedicated capacity and Private VPC deployment (Sergio to provide)

3) Calendar: we have the two time windows you suggested: Tue 2028-03-27 10:00–11:00 PT (preferred for our security team) and Wed 2028-03-28 14:00–15:00 PT. I’ll hold Tue 3/27 tentatively and will send a calendar invite once Marcus confirms availability for the BAA discussion.

Acceptance items / Questions for you before the call:
- Please confirm whether the 365-day audit log retention is a hard requirement or a preferred target.
- If you require an on-prem connector rather than a cloud Private VPC, let us know and we’ll include ops notes in the sizing.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
